ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives four candidate substances and structural formulas: methanol (methanol) contains one hydroxyl group -OH; propane (propane) is a hydrocarbon containing only C-C and C-H bonds; ethene (ethene) is a hydrocarbon containing C=C and C-H bonds; ethanal (ethanal) contains one carbonyl group C=O, and the molecule is relatively small. Reasoning: Water is a polar molecule and can be mutually soluble with molecules that can form hydrogen bonds or have obvious polarity. Methanol, because it contains a hydroxyl group, has strong polarity and can form hydrogen bonds with water, so it is very likely to be mutually soluble with water. Ethanal, because it contains a carbonyl group, the carbonyl oxygen can accept hydrogen bonds from water, and the molecule is relatively small, so it is also relatively likely to be mutually soluble with water. Propane and ethene are nonpolar hydrocarbons and are not easily mutually soluble with water. Therefore, methanol and ethanal should be selected.

method.method_draft: From the image, list each candidate and its key structural feature. Mark methanol as highly polar because of its hydroxyl group and ability to hydrogen bond with water. Mark ethanal as polar because its carbonyl group can accept hydrogen bonds from water and the molecule is small. Mark propane and ethene as nonpolar hydrocarbons, so they are not likely miscible with water. Therefore select methanol and ethanal.
